dominant_strengths: Serif headline 'Delete this project?' adds editorial gravity that elevates an otherwise utilitarian destructive-action dialog.
Clear information hierarchy: project chip, consequences list, type-to-confirm input, and primary destructive button each get distinct zones.
Restrained red accent reserved for icon, 'Will delete' tag, X markers, and CTA — semantic color used with discipline.
dominant_weaknesses: Cancel button blends into the dark canvas with weak border contrast, undermining the safe-default escape route in a destructive flow.
The four 'what gets deleted' rows all use identical red X glyphs, flattening severity and missing a chance to weight irreversibility.
Layout is conventional vertical stack — no spatial idea differentiates this from a stock shadcn destructive-confirmation modal.
fix_priorities: Strengthen Cancel button affordance (lighter fill or border) so the non-destructive path reads as the safer default.
Add subtle motion/state cues: input validation glow, button enabling only after correct text, micro-animation on the trash icon.
Differentiate the consequence list with counts/iconography variation to give the warning real informational density.
Tighten typographic rhythm between serif H1 and the body — the body feels generic sans against the editorial heading.
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral clarity (typed confirmation, explicit consequences) leads, visceral is competent via serif and red restraint, reflective payoff is modest because the pattern feels familiar.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it executes a careful destructive-confirmation modal with friction, consequence transparency, and tonal seriousness, though without a distinctive idea beyond polish.
